must_observe: Creates exactly one canonical workstream folder under the supplied temporary root
Captures outcome, scope, acceptance, both workspaces, and the backend-to-frontend contract dependency
Defines bounded backend and frontend backlog work items with ownership, readiness, lifecycle, acceptance, verification, and expected receipts
Includes a structured verification contract with default targeted depth, claim-level required evidence, and a producer-consumer integration gate
Uses the default capture mode and leaves the new tasks in lifecycle backlog without starting a worker or making a delivery change
Orders or gates frontend integration on an explicit backend schema version while allowing only justified parallel work
Keeps shared context writes with the lead and requires workers to return receipts
Defines a future integrated partial-failure verification rather than accepting two local success claims
Reports backlog, readiness, scheduling state, decisions, and remaining work without claiming simulated work is complete
must_not_observe: Creates one context folder per repository
Lets workers edit shared context files directly
Treats independent task support as permission for operations outside the user request
Schedules or executes a task during the capture turn
Closes or archives the workstream after planning
